answer: Sybil resistance rests on proof-of-space-time tied to a cost-bonded identity. A seat needs unique disk sealed for a term plus a bond at the same address. Each identity maps to storage that cannot be copied, so a thousand fake accounts need a thousand commitments and stakes. Yield grows along one vine of sealed plots, not by spawning handles, and replacement costs fresh sealing plus slashing risk. Capital idles while the epoch clock runs toward a re-sampled horizon, and duplicates fall to an atlas of cross-checks. Doubling the attack doubles real outlay in storage, energy and locked tokens.
